best_field_traits: Basal winter rosette of shorter, broader blades; spring flowering culms and autumn secondary branches can look dramatically different.
Open spring panicle commonly about 4–13 cm long; later branch heads can be small and partly sheathed.
Lance-shaped stem blades often 3–14 cm long and 3–12 mm wide.
Ligule fringe of hairs about 1–4.2 mm long in broad treatments.
Sheaths range from nearly smooth to coarse hairy, sometimes with raised tubercle/pustule bases; avoid identifying from sheath hair alone.
Mature spikelets commonly 2.9–4 mm; lower glume is shorter than entire spikelet.
crew_field_check: 1. Confirm original photo ROLE (flower macro, habitat view, or open panicle) before using a label; this image alone is NOT a verified same-plant key.
2. On living same-plant shoot find spring basal rosette and compare early spring versus late-season leafy secondary shoots.
3. Open the collar: photograph true hair-fringe ligule separately from hairs at the blade base, with mm scale.

4. Measure at least three mature ripe SPIKELETS with 1-mm ruler; size categories ~1.3–1.6 lindheimeri, 2.1–3.2 commutatum, ~2.9–4 oligosanthes, ~3–3.5 pedicellatum, but overlapping ranges prohibit pure size-only identification.
5. If rosette/collar/leaf base or mature spikelet dimensions unavailable, record Dichanthelium sp. and a source-determined tentative species.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Winter rosette / whole rooted tuft, followed by same clump spring full panicle
Three ripe spikelets 2.9–4 mm under calibrated scale and separate glumes
Blade/sheath ligule 1–4 mm fringe with mm reference, showing actual collar versus leaf-base cilia
Leaf sheath hairs and swollen hair bases photographed with accurate side-light

confused_with: other Dichanthelium species (not yet represented in this learner)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with D. lindheimeri, ripe spikelets are much larger (~2.9–4 vs 1.3–1.6 mm); compared with D. pedicellatum (~3–3.5 mm), lengths overlap and true collar fringe plus leaf widths are critical. D. commutatum may have broad/cordate stem blade bases and minute/absent true ligule. Don't force the identity from one branching inflorescence.
comparisons.photo_context: Four real already archived source-labelled images are incorporated into a genus comparison. The Lindheimer habitat photo does not display a measured spikelet; none proves collar/leaf base anatomy. Morphological ranges are literature-based, not measured from these photographs.
not_reliable_alone: Airy panicle silhouette in a single season
Habitat or presumed annual/perennial condition from clipped stem
Ligule hair lengths or spikelet sizes inferred from photos without rulers
The older D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri name interpreted as a new separate species

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Rosette panicgrass — see photo evidence, then check the plant
steps: First real live growth photo at gallery panel 7 (index 6): field tuft with leaf blades in rocky habitat. The lower ROOTS are NOT exposed, and no established winter overwintering rosette is visible.
Panels 8–9 (indices 7,8) now show two authentic angles of an open many-pedicelled panicle and oval attached spikelets. The hand is scale context, NOT a 1-mm ruler. Arrow only real axis/spikelet.
Panel 2 (index 1) independently shows true source-labelled attached spikelets. Neither individual glume nor a sterile/fertile lemma is physically separated; need true dissection with mm ruler.

Actual INNER blade/sheath ligule (hair fringe ~1–3 mm according to Flora of North America; sometimes broader treatment 1–4.2mm) is STILL missing. No collar macro in images. Do not mistake blade-edge/sheath exterior hairs.

Other-taxonomic-species photos at indices 3–5 are comparisons of D. commutatum, D. lindheimeri, D. pedicellatum, not tissue from oligosanthes. The historical illustration (index 2) is NOT a photographed diagnostic role.

For final field-grade species confidence: same source authenticated basal winter rosette to flowering culm, inner 1-mm-calibrated hair ligule, 3 ripe separately measured 2.7–4.2-mm spikelets and exposed lower/upper glumes plus sterile/fertile lemma.

One additional expert photo-guided set of D. oligosanthes leaves/spikelets identified; photo-specific reproduction licenses UNDER AUDIT and not installed. Bob Harms D. oligosanthes var. scribnerianum ligule plate is a DISTINCT variety, not a definitive identity photo here.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Panicles often overlap. Show spring/autumn phase, true leaf collar, and at least three mature measured spikelets from the same plant before a firm species call.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.short: Open spring panicle PLUS rooted winter rosette
field_id_short_tiles.details: Find an open, airy spring panicle with distinct oval spikelets, then trace the SAME perennial plant back to its basal rosette. Seasonal leafy autumn branches can look different. Existing photos show actual branching and spikelets but do not establish a connected winter rosette or measured anatomy.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PANICLE PHOTO PRESENT; MATCHED ROOTED ROSETTE MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · OPEN THE COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: True hair-fringe ligule commonly about 1–4 mm
field_id_short_tiles.details: At the INSIDE blade–sheath junction inspect the actual fringe of hairs; published descriptions vary by taxon treatment, roughly 1–4.2 mm (about 1–3 mm in a narrower treatment). Separate ligule hairs from leaf-edge cilia and sheath hairs. A 1-mm ruler and side-lit 10–20× macro are required for an anatomical arrow.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED RANGE; TRUE LIGULE MACRO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE THREE RIPE SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.details: Measure at least three mature spikelets from one source-verified plant; Kew describes 2.9–4-mm-long, 1.2–2.2-mm-wide awnless spikelets. An open panicle without a scale cannot distinguish this species from D. pedicellatum. Each spikelet has a lower sterile and upper fertile floret.
field_id_short_tiles.status: LITERATURE SIZE; MEASURED ATTACHED SPIKELETS MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · FIND BOTH GLUMES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower glume about 0.8–2.2 mm; upper near full length
field_id_short_tiles.details: Kew's broad species treatment gives a LOWER glume about 0.8–2.2 mm (roughly one-quarter to one-half the spikelet), with 1–3 veins, and an UPPER glume about as long as the spikelet with about five veins. Do not label upper glume or vein counts unless the photographed bract is actually separated and in focus. Narrow subspecies descriptions can give smaller lower-glume ranges.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED GLUME RANGES; DISSECTION/VEIN ARROWS MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · OPEN THE TWO FLORETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower sterile lemma thin; upper fertile lemma hardened
field_id_short_tiles.details: The lower sterile lemma resembles the upper glume and is approximately spikelet-length with about five veins; a reduced sterile palea may be present. The UPPER fertile lemma is hardened and approximately 2.9–4 mm in Kew's broad treatment, with a firm palea inside. Both florets are AWNLESS. Dissect one mature spikelet and show each bract separately before drawing labels.
field_id_short_tiles.status: LITERATURE ANATOMY; INDIVIDUAL LEMMA PHOTOS MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · RULE OUT NEARBY DICHANTHELIUM
field_id_short_tiles.short: Pedicellatum overlaps; measure ligule and base
field_id_short_tiles.details: D. pedicellatum overlaps in spikelet size (roughly 3–3.5 mm) but the Williamson County treatment describes a small cormlike base, no winter rosette, and a very short 0.25–0.5-mm hair ligule. D. lindheimeri usually has much smaller ripe spikelets (about 1.3–1.7 mm); D. commutatum may have broad heart-based leaves and a minute or absent true ligule. Use the same plant's rooted base, collar and ripe spikelets together.
field_id_short_tiles.status: COMPARISONS WRITTEN; MATCHED ORGAN PHOTOS MISSING
